# Chat Input Scope

## How To Build

A ChatInputScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ChatInputScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well as snippets of Piton.

### Shape

#### Description

Input on the left, send button on the right.
<Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to the HarnessIntegrationScope
Sending sends the prompt in the selected tab's mode, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. While the harness is working, the send button on the Code, Chain, Spec, and Freeform tabs reads "Queue", since the prompt will queue. On the Ask tab it always reads "Send", because a question is never queued. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

#### Instructions

- [ChatInputInstruction](../../../shape/ChatInput.md#chat-input-instruction)

#### Send Options

##### Split Button

The send button is a split button: the send or queue button itself, and joined to its right, a narrow half with a chevron that opens a menu of other ways to send the prompt, above the button, its right edge lined up with the button's. The chevron half is disabled whenever the send half is, and while a preview shows, and its tooltip says it shows more ways to send, with its shortcut.

##### Keyboard

<Ctrl+Shift+Enter> (<Cmd+Shift+Enter> on macOS) in the chat input opens the menu with its first option highlighted, and does nothing while the input is empty or a preview shows. While it is open, the text keeps focus, <Up> and <Down> move the highlight, wrapping around, <Enter> picks the highlighted option, and <Escape> closes the menu, as does pressing <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> again or the mouse anywhere outside it. Each option highlights on hover, and clicking one picks it.

##### Options

The menu's options, in order:

- "Preview Compiled Prompt", with an eye icon
- "Queue", with a list icon, which queues the prompt rather than sending it, even while the harness is free, as the queue of the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor) says; like the send button, it clears the input. On the Ask tab it is disabled, since a question never queues, and the highlight passes over it
- "Send to task", with a send icon, only while a task is running with a harness that can be fed more, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, and its output is shown, the previous tasks not expanded over it; never on the Ask tab, where a question runs on its own. It sends what is typed, and what is attached, to the running task instead of queueing it, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, and clears the input as sending does. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) still queues, as the send button does

#### Editing Queued

Editing a queued prompt, from the queue of the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor), sets aside the prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab, and puts the queued prompt's text in the input, its attachments above it, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of the text. Above the attachments, a row with a pencil icon reads "Editing queued prompt N", its place in the queue, and at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel" (with ⌘ on macOS). The send button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and the send menu isn't offered.
Everything in the input works as ever while editing, tabs included. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or Save, saves the edit, in the tab selected then, and <Escape>, when nothing else in the input takes it, cancels it. Either way, the prompt that was set aside comes back just as it was. Saving an empty prompt isn't possible, just as sending one isn't. Editing another queued prompt meanwhile first cancels the edit in progress; so does switching projects.

#### Preview

Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with, at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.
The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape> goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.

#### Tabs

##### Overview

The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using gpui-kit's default tab styling. There is a tab for each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), in their order: Code, Chain, Spec, Ask, and Freeform. Code, Spec, Ask, and Freeform are ordinary tabs. Chain is also a tab, just a small one, because it only shows an icon. All five sit flush against each other with no extra gaps, and no tab has more padding than a normal tab.
The chat input starts in the combined mode: Chain is selected, so Code and Spec are selected together, and a prompt sent before switching tabs changes the code and the spec together.
Pressing <Ctrl+Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to Chain to Spec to Ask to Freeform and back to Code, <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> the other way, and focus remains in the chat input. It is <Ctrl> on macOS too, not <Cmd>.
<Tab> and <Shift+Tab> don't switch tabs, and don't indent the text

###### Either

they move keyboard focus out of the chat input to the next

or previous control, as they do everywhere else. While the completion menu is open, <Tab> is still the menu's.

##### Chain

Chain is a tab with unusual behaviour. It shows an icon rather than a label, reading "Code and Spec" as its tooltip, and selecting it selects both Code and Spec. It never shows a focus outline, and its icon looks evenly spaced between Code and Spec whichever of the two is selected.
Unselected, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and sits between Code and Spec like any other tab, overlapping neither of them.
In combined mode, with Chain selected, Chain has no line along its bottom, just as the joined Code and Spec beneath it have none. In separate mode, unselected, it has one, like any other unselected

###### Tab

the tab bar's bottom line runs beneath it, the same colour and

thickness, in the same place, as beneath any other unselected tab, at any display scale. This holds at every window size and display scale, in light and dark mode: in combined mode nothing draws a line beneath Chain at all, rather than a line being drawn and then hidden, since a hidden line can show again wherever rounding to the display's pixels uncovers it.
Selected, it shows a joined chain at full opacity. Selecting it animates as though it took a margin of -50% of its own width on both its left and right sides: Code and Spec slide together until they meet underneath it, so it ends up sitting on top of both. Deselecting it animates them apart again. While Chain is selected, Code and Spec both show as selected and read as a single unified tab, with no line between them. Chain itself has a transparent background and no left or right borders, so the joined Code and Spec show through underneath it.

##### Help

To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of help text says what the selected tab is for, and changes as soon as another tab is selected. It is extra small and dimmer than muted text, set a little apart from the last tab, so it reads as a quiet note about the tab rather than as another tab. It is cut off rather than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.
It reads what the selected tab's mode is for, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says.

##### Session

At the far right of the bar, at the right end of the help text, sits how much context the selected tab's conversation holds, then a New conversation button. The questions of the Ask tab have a conversation of their own, and the other tabs share the tasks', as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, so the figure is the Ask tab's conversation while it is selected, and the tasks' on any other tab.
The figure reads "Context", then the number of tokens, short and extra small, muted: "850", "42.1k", "123k", or "1.2M", to a decimal place below a hundred of a unit. It follows each reply as the harness reports it. While the next prompt would start a new conversation, as when the project has none yet or New conversation was just pressed, it reads "Context 0". Its tooltip says how many tokens the conversation the next prompt carries on holds, or that the next prompt starts a new conversation.
New conversation is a small ghost button with a sparkles icon, reading "New conversation". Pressing it starts a new conversation for the selected tab: the tasks' on Code, Chain, Spec, and Freeform, the questions' on Ask. The next run in that tab, or in any tab sharing its conversation, starts a new one with no context instead of carrying on, and the figure reads "Context 0". A run of the conversation left that is still going finishes as it would, but neither it nor the project's history brings that conversation back, even once the project is closed and opened again, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says.
It can be pressed while a run in that conversation is under way, a task on Code, Chain, Spec, or Freeform, or any question on Ask, without waiting for it to finish. Pressed while a task runs, the prompts sent meanwhile queue as ever, and the next task to run from the queue, the first in it, starts a new conversation with no context, the ones after it carrying that one on. That holds even when the running task is the first of its conversation and the harness hasn't yet said which conversation it is: once it does, it isn't carried on either.
Its tooltip says which conversation it resets: "Start a new conversation for tasks" or "Start a new conversation for questions", adding, while a run in it is under way, that the run finishes in the conversation left. It is disabled only while that conversation has nothing to carry on and no run in it is under way, its tooltip then saying the next task, or question, already starts a new conversation.
Both sit on the bar's bottom line, which runs beneath them as it does beneath the help text, and neither is cut off: the help text gives way to them when the bar is narrow.

##### Usage

Just right of the context figure, before New conversation, sits the agent's usage: how much of the harness picked, of the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope), has been used, as Claude Code's /usage shows it. Its summary is short and extra small, muted like the context figure: "Usage", then the share used of the plan limit nearest to running out, such as "Usage 42%", turning the theme's warning colour from 80% and its error colour once the limit is reached. When the harness reports no plan limits, the summary is the cost of this project's runs since it was opened, such as "Usage $1.24", or the tokens they used, as the context figure is written, when it reports no cost either. Until anything has been reported, it reads "Usage", with nothing after it.
Clicking the summary opens a popover above it with all the details, each group headed, and each figure labelled:
- Plan limits: each limit the harness reports, such as the current
  session's and the week's, with the share used as a bar and a
  percentage, and when it resets.
- Conversation: the context the selected tab's conversation holds,
  and its input, output, cache-read, and cache-written tokens, and
  its cost.
- This project: the same totals for every run in the project since
  it was opened, tasks and questions, and how many runs there were.
- The harness and model the figures came from, and when they were
  last reported.
A group, or a figure, the harness doesn't report is left out rather than shown as zero, and when nothing has been reported the popover says so. The figures come from what the harness reports as its runs go, never from running anything of its own to ask, and update in place while the popover is open, following each reply. Clicking outside the popover, or pressing Escape, closes it. The summary's tooltip says to click for the details. Like the context figure, it is never cut off: the help text gives way to it.

##### Slice

Just left of the context figure sits the Slice toggle: a small ghost button with a scissors icon, reading "Slice", which shows as selected while it is on. It starts off. Its tooltip says what the prompt is sent as: while off, the prompt written as a spec, its references linking to the spec they name; while on, the prompt with the `piton slice` of each spec it references. Clicking it turns it on or off, and it applies to every tab, Ask included. It stays as it is across sends, tab switches, and project switches, as the prompt being written does, and the help text gives way to it as it does to the session controls.

##### Colour

The selected tab and the tab body holding the input are tinted the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope). With Chain selected, Code, Spec, and the body are all purple. The colour transitions smoothly whenever the selected tab changes, straight from the old tab's colour to the new one's. The tabs wrap around, so pressing <Ctrl+Tab> on Freeform fades grey straight to Code's red, and <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> on Code fades red straight to Freeform's grey; neither lights up Chain, Spec, or Ask on the way. A fade to or from Freeform's grey keeps the other tab's hue, only draining or filling its colour, so it never passes through another hue.
The send button, both its halves, takes the same colour as the selected tab, purple with Chain selected, but at full strength rather than as a tint, so it stands out against the tinted body. Its label and chevron are in the theme's text colour for a solid hue, and the line between its halves is only faintly darker or lighter than it, half as far as its hover, just enough to part them. Disabled, the button fades as a disabled button does, in the same colour, and the line fades with the half it borders, never staying solid across a faded button.

#### System Prompt

The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode's system prompt is sent with it, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says.

#### Ask

Ask is for simply asking a question, which runs as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says. Any number of questions can be asked, and they all run at the same time; asking another never stops or waits for one already running.
Each question's progress and results are shown in a [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope). The questions stack directly above the tabs, the newest nearest them, in a column that pushes the message list up to make room rather than covering it, so none of a running task's progress is ever hidden behind them. Each slides up out of the chat input with an animation as it is asked, the message list giving way above it. While the harness works on a question, it is a single row showing the latest thing the harness did. A finished question is a row with its status and first line.
However many questions are asked, the stack is only as tall as its rows, up to 240 pixels, the queue's most, and scrolls beyond that with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), kept on the newest question, nearest the tabs, as each is asked. Once it holds more than fit, the stack lays out only the rows in view, as a table does, so a long stack costs no more to show, scroll, or animate than a short one, and the drawer's bottom follows the stack's top as ever.
Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status and first line, above its full task table, in the [AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope), which it fills, the table scrolling once it is taller, with its lock to the bottom off to start with. Only one question is open at a time: opening another closes the one open back down to its row. An open question leaves the stack for the drawer. Clicking an open question's heading closes it down to its row in the stack, and clicking a finished question's row opens it again. Each question has a close button, which removes it and stops it if it is still running, leaving the others running. A closed question becomes a previous answer.

#### Answer Steps

For a question, only the answer matters, so wherever a finished question's task table is shown, an open question and a previous answer, the table collapses the steps leading up to the answer, as the [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A question closed into the previous answers starts collapsed again. Tasks are never collapsed like this: see the [MessageList](../message-list/index.md#message-list).

#### Previous Answers

Previous answers are a [HistoryListScope](../../../ui/components/history-list/index.md#history-list-scope), shown only while the Ask tab is selected, at the top of the questions stacked above the tabs. It lists every question asked before and closed: those saved with the project and those closed since. Its row reads "No previous answers", "1 previous answer", or "N previous answers", and while expanded, "Back to the questions". Each previous answer offers Resend, which asks its question again, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. Expanded, the row and the list go into the [AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope), sliding up from on top of any question rows still in the stack. The questions asked from now on carry on the conversation the latest of them left off.

#### Answer Drawer

[AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope)

#### Selecting Answer Text

The text of an answer being viewed, in the answer drawer, whether an open question or a previous answer, can be selected by dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the drawer shows a [SelectionPopoverScope](../../../ui/components/selection-popover/index.md#selection-popover-scope) with two buttons: "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon.
Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard. Attach to prompt adds it to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the selection. The popover also closes when the drawer closes.

#### Attachments

What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.
Images can be attached too: pasted from the clipboard while the chat input has focus, dropped onto the chat input from the file manager, or chosen with a small ghost button with an image icon, whose tooltip says "Attach images", on the tab row between the last tab and the help text, which opens the platform's file picker for any files, several at once, since the picker can't be limited to images. Pasting an image attaches it rather than putting anything in the text, even when the clipboard holds text as well; every image on the clipboard is attached, and a clipboard with no image pastes its text as usual. Several files dropped or chosen at once are attached in their order, each on its own merits. An image is known by its content, not its name, and only PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP are taken: anything else pasted, dropped, or chosen, BMP, TIFF, and SVG included, is not attached, and a warning notification titled "Not attached" says it isn't an image. An image larger than 5 MB is not attached either, and the same notification says it is too large. A folder dropped or chosen isn't an image either, and a file that can't be read is not attached, the same notification saying it couldn't be read, and why. Each file left out has its own notification, and the others are still attached.
Files can be dropped only on the chat input itself, its tabs, the attachments, and the text input; dropping them on the message list above it does nothing. While files are dragged over the chat input, its background is highlighted with the accent's fill, laid about a quarter of the way over it.
An attached image's row shows a small thumbnail, its file name, or "Pasted image" for one pasted, and its size in pixels, muted, with the same remove button; hovering the thumbnail shows the image larger, at most 320 pixels. Images and text are listed together in the order they were attached while the prompt is written. A prompt taken back into the input, as when a queued prompt is edited, lists its text first, then its images, each image named by its saved file, a pasted one included.
Attachments belong to the prompt being written, not to a tab: switching tabs keeps them all, and they go with the prompt whichever tab it is sent from. When the prompt is sent, its attachments are sent along with it and the list empties, as the text input does. A queued prompt keeps the attachments it was sent with.

#### Projects

The questions stacked above the tabs, the open answer, and the previous answers belong to their project, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says: switching projects shows those of the project switched to, while the questions of other projects carry on running in the background. The prompt being written, its attachments, the selected tab, and the Slice toggle stay as they are across a switch, and are sent to the project on screen.

#### Escape

Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat input. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) brings it back, from anywhere the chat input isn't beneath something else, as the [MainWindowScope](../../application/MainWindow.md#main-window-scope) says.

#### Grow To Fit

The text input is a [GrowingTextInputScope](../../../ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input-scope) growing to 12 rows at most. Its single row lines up with the send button.

#### Auto Focus

The chat input should be auto-focused.

#### Syntax Highlighting

Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

#### Lsp

[LSP](../../lsp/index.md#lsp)

#### Harness Mentions

```
overview: Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@` offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself. The placeholder mentions both.
trigger: A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter, digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one they never reach the [LSP](../../lsp/index.md#lsp).

Results are narrowed and ordered like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before matches anywhere in it, then by name.
accepting: Accepting one inserts it as a mention, as the [HarnessCatalogScope](../../harness-integration/catalog/index.md#harness-catalog-scope) says, in place of what was typed of it. Mentions work without the [LSP](../../lsp/index.md#lsp).
```

#### Hidden Anchor

While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes, they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope)

##### Escaping

A prompt may hold anything, text pasted into it included, so it isn't written into the anchor as Piton prose, where braces, colons, leading dashes, code fences, comments, indentation, and backslashes all mean something. The anchor is exported, so that it compiles, and its userPrompt is a multi-line escape block, which Piton keeps exactly as it is: the prompt's lines, each at the block's indentation, fenced by a line of three backslashes, or of one more than any line of the prompt made only of backslashes, so nothing in it closes the block early. The systemPrompt is written the same way.
Each at-brace or dollar-brace around a dotted path of identifiers whose first name is imported, in the userPrompt and then the systemPrompt, is also listed once, in the order they first appear, as an item of the anchor's references property, left out when there are none; a reference to a name that isn't imported, such as a pasted shell variable, is only text. `piton compile` resolves the references. What the harness receives is the prompt as it was saved, line for line, with each reference replaced by what it resolved to: a dollar-brace by its text, and an at-brace by a Markdown link, from the project directory, to the reference document the project's build writes for it, in the reference root of the config's first adapter, such as .claude/reference, named by its dotted path, and going to the heading for the anchor or property it names once the document is built. A prompt saved by an earlier version, as quoted pieces or as prose, still reads back.

##### Auto Imports

The names a prompt uses are imported however the prompt got there, typed, completed, or pasted. What `piton lsp` is shown while the prompt is typed is the prompt as prose, line for line and position for position as typed, but with anything outside a reference other than letters, digits, and spaces between words blanked out, character for character. Pasted text with an unclosed quote or brace, a code fence, deeper indentation, or what would be a comment then never stops the server finding the names that need importing, both as completions are offered and when the prompt is sent.

##### Attached Text

A prompt with attached text gives the hidden anchor an attachedText

1	# Chat Input Scope
2	
3	## How To Build
4	
5	A ChatInputScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ChatInputScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.
6	
7	## Theme
8	
9	Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.
10	
11	## Concept
12	
13	### Pitch
14	
15	A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well as snippets of Piton.
16	
17	### Shape
18	
19	#### Description
20	
21	Input on the left, send button on the right.
22	<Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to the HarnessIntegrationScope
23	Sending sends the prompt in the selected tab's mode, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. While the harness is working, the send button on the Code, Chain, Spec, and Freeform tabs reads "Queue", since the prompt will queue. On the Ask tab it always reads "Send", because a question is never queued. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.
24	
25	#### Instructions
26	
27	- [ChatInputInstruction](../../../shape/ChatInput.md#chat-input-instruction)
28	
29	#### Send Options
30	
31	##### Split Button
32	
33	The send button is a split button: the send or queue button itself, and joined to its right, a narrow half with a chevron that opens a menu of other ways to send the prompt, above the button, its right edge lined up with the button's. The chevron half is disabled whenever the send half is, and while a preview shows, and its tooltip says it shows more ways to send, with its shortcut.
34	
35	##### Keyboard
36	
37	<Ctrl+Shift+Enter> (<Cmd+Shift+Enter> on macOS) in the chat input opens the menu with its first option highlighted, and does nothing while the input is empty or a preview shows. While it is open, the text keeps focus, <Up> and <Down> move the highlight, wrapping around, <Enter> picks the highlighted option, and <Escape> closes the menu, as does pressing <Ctrl+Shift+Enter> again or the mouse anywhere outside it. Each option highlights on hover, and clicking one picks it.
38	
39	##### Options
40	
41	The menu's options, in order:
42	
43	- "Preview Compiled Prompt", with an eye icon
44	- "Queue", with a list icon, which queues the prompt rather than sending it, even while the harness is free, as the queue of the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor) says; like the send button, it clears the input. On the Ask tab it is disabled, since a question never queues, and the highlight passes over it
45	- "Send to task", with a send icon, only while a task is running with a harness that can be fed more, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, and its output is shown, the previous tasks not expanded over it; never on the Ask tab, where a question runs on its own. It sends what is typed, and what is attached, to the running task instead of queueing it, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, and clears the input as sending does. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) still queues, as the send button does
46	
47	#### Editing Queued
48	
49	Editing a queued prompt, from the queue of the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor), sets aside the prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab, and puts the queued prompt's text in the input, its attachments above it, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of the text. Above the attachments, a row with a pencil icon reads "Editing queued prompt N", its place in the queue, and at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel" (with ⌘ on macOS). The send button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and the send menu isn't offered.
50	Everything in the input works as ever while editing, tabs included. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or Save, saves the edit, in the tab selected then, and <Escape>, when nothing else in the input takes it, cancels it. Either way, the prompt that was set aside comes back just as it was. Saving an empty prompt isn't possible, just as sending one isn't. Editing another queued prompt meanwhile first cancels the edit in progress; so does switching projects.
51	
52	#### Preview
53	
54	Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with, at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.
55	The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape> goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.
56	
57	#### Tabs
58	
59	##### Overview
60	
61	The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using gpui-kit's default tab styling. There is a tab for each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), in their order: Code, Chain, Spec, Ask, and Freeform. Code, Spec, Ask, and Freeform are ordinary tabs. Chain is also a tab, just a small one, because it only shows an icon. All five sit flush against each other with no extra gaps, and no tab has more padding than a normal tab.
62	The chat input starts in the combined mode: Chain is selected, so Code and Spec are selected together, and a prompt sent before switching tabs changes the code and the spec together.
63	Pressing <Ctrl+Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to Chain to Spec to Ask to Freeform and back to Code, <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> the other way, and focus remains in the chat input. It is <Ctrl> on macOS too, not <Cmd>.
64	<Tab> and <Shift+Tab> don't switch tabs, and don't indent the text
65	
66	###### Either
67	
68	they move keyboard focus out of the chat input to the next
69	
70	or previous control, as they do everywhere else. While the completion menu is open, <Tab> is still the menu's.
71	
72	##### Chain
73	
74	Chain is a tab with unusual behaviour. It shows an icon rather than a label, reading "Code and Spec" as its tooltip, and selecting it selects both Code and Spec. It never shows a focus outline, and its icon looks evenly spaced between Code and Spec whichever of the two is selected.
75	Unselected, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and sits between Code and Spec like any other tab, overlapping neither of them.
76	In combined mode, with Chain selected, Chain has no line along its bottom, just as the joined Code and Spec beneath it have none. In separate mode, unselected, it has one, like any other unselected
77	
78	###### Tab
79	
80	the tab bar's bottom line runs beneath it, the same colour and
81	
82	thickness, in the same place, as beneath any other unselected tab, at any display scale. This holds at every window size and display scale, in light and dark mode: in combined mode nothing draws a line beneath Chain at all, rather than a line being drawn and then hidden, since a hidden line can show again wherever rounding to the display's pixels uncovers it.
83	Selected, it shows a joined chain at full opacity. Selecting it animates as though it took a margin of -50% of its own width on both its left and right sides: Code and Spec slide together until they meet underneath it, so it ends up sitting on top of both. Deselecting it animates them apart again. While Chain is selected, Code and Spec both show as selected and read as a single unified tab, with no line between them. Chain itself has a transparent background and no left or right borders, so the joined Code and Spec show through underneath it.
84	
85	##### Help
86	
87	To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of help text says what the selected tab is for, and changes as soon as another tab is selected. It is extra small and dimmer than muted text, set a little apart from the last tab, so it reads as a quiet note about the tab rather than as another tab. It is cut off rather than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.
88	It reads what the selected tab's mode is for, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says.
89	
90	##### Session
91	
92	At the far right of the bar, at the right end of the help text, sits how much context the selected tab's conversation holds, then a New conversation button. The questions of the Ask tab have a conversation of their own, and the other tabs share the tasks', as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, so the figure is the Ask tab's conversation while it is selected, and the tasks' on any other tab.
93	The figure reads "Context", then the number of tokens, short and extra small, muted: "850", "42.1k", "123k", or "1.2M", to a decimal place below a hundred of a unit. It follows each reply as the harness reports it. While the next prompt would start a new conversation, as when the project has none yet or New conversation was just pressed, it reads "Context 0". Its tooltip says how many tokens the conversation the next prompt carries on holds, or that the next prompt starts a new conversation.
94	New conversation is a small ghost button with a sparkles icon, reading "New conversation". Pressing it starts a new conversation for the selected tab: the tasks' on Code, Chain, Spec, and Freeform, the questions' on Ask. The next run in that tab, or in any tab sharing its conversation, starts a new one with no context instead of carrying on, and the figure reads "Context 0". A run of the conversation left that is still going finishes as it would, but neither it nor the project's history brings that conversation back, even once the project is closed and opened again, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says.
95	It can be pressed while a run in that conversation is under way, a task on Code, Chain, Spec, or Freeform, or any question on Ask, without waiting for it to finish. Pressed while a task runs, the prompts sent meanwhile queue as ever, and the next task to run from the queue, the first in it, starts a new conversation with no context, the ones after it carrying that one on. That holds even when the running task is the first of its conversation and the harness hasn't yet said which conversation it is: once it does, it isn't carried on either.
96	Its tooltip says which conversation it resets: "Start a new conversation for tasks" or "Start a new conversation for questions", adding, while a run in it is under way, that the run finishes in the conversation left. It is disabled only while that conversation has nothing to carry on and no run in it is under way, its tooltip then saying the next task, or question, already starts a new conversation.
97	Both sit on the bar's bottom line, which runs beneath them as it does beneath the help text, and neither is cut off: the help text gives way to them when the bar is narrow.
98	
99	##### Usage
100	
101	Just right of the context figure, before New conversation, sits the agent's usage: how much of the harness picked, of the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope), has been used, as Claude Code's /usage shows it. Its summary is short and extra small, muted like the context figure: "Usage", then the share used of the plan limit nearest to running out, such as "Usage 42%", turning the theme's warning colour from 80% and its error colour once the limit is reached. When the harness reports no plan limits, the summary is the cost of this project's runs since it was opened, such as "Usage $1.24", or the tokens they used, as the context figure is written, when it reports no cost either. Until anything has been reported, it reads "Usage", with nothing after it.
102	Clicking the summary opens a popover above it with all the details, each group headed, and each figure labelled:
103	- Plan limits: each limit the harness reports, such as the current
104	  session's and the week's, with the share used as a bar and a
105	  percentage, and when it resets.
106	- Conversation: the context the selected tab's conversation holds,
107	  and its input, output, cache-read, and cache-written tokens, and
108	  its cost.
109	- This project: the same totals for every run in the project since
110	  it was opened, tasks and questions, and how many runs there were.
111	- The harness and model the figures came from, and when they were
112	  last reported.
113	A group, or a figure, the harness doesn't report is left out rather than shown as zero, and when nothing has been reported the popover says so. The figures come from what the harness reports as its runs go, never from running anything of its own to ask, and update in place while the popover is open, following each reply. Clicking outside the popover, or pressing Escape, closes it. The summary's tooltip says to click for the details. Like the context figure, it is never cut off: the help text gives way to it.
114	
115	##### Slice
116	
117	Just left of the context figure sits the Slice toggle: a small ghost button with a scissors icon, reading "Slice", which shows as selected while it is on. It starts off. Its tooltip says what the prompt is sent as: while off, the prompt written as a spec, its references linking to the spec they name; while on, the prompt with the `piton slice` of each spec it references. Clicking it turns it on or off, and it applies to every tab, Ask included. It stays as it is across sends, tab switches, and project switches, as the prompt being written does, and the help text gives way to it as it does to the session controls.
118	
119	##### Colour
120	
121	The selected tab and the tab body holding the input are tinted the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope). With Chain selected, Code, Spec, and the body are all purple. The colour transitions smoothly whenever the selected tab changes, straight from the old tab's colour to the new one's. The tabs wrap around, so pressing <Ctrl+Tab> on Freeform fades grey straight to Code's red, and <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> on Code fades red straight to Freeform's grey; neither lights up Chain, Spec, or Ask on the way. A fade to or from Freeform's grey keeps the other tab's hue, only draining or filling its colour, so it never passes through another hue.
122	The send button, both its halves, takes the same colour as the selected tab, purple with Chain selected, but at full strength rather than as a tint, so it stands out against the tinted body. Its label and chevron are in the theme's text colour for a solid hue, and the line between its halves is only faintly darker or lighter than it, half as far as its hover, just enough to part them. Disabled, the button fades as a disabled button does, in the same colour, and the line fades with the half it borders, never staying solid across a faded button.
123	
124	#### System Prompt
125	
126	The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode's system prompt is sent with it, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says.
127	
128	#### Ask
129	
130	Ask is for simply asking a question, which runs as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says. Any number of questions can be asked, and they all run at the same time; asking another never stops or waits for one already running.
131	Each question's progress and results are shown in a [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope). The questions stack directly above the tabs, the newest nearest them, in a column that pushes the message list up to make room rather than covering it, so none of a running task's progress is ever hidden behind them. Each slides up out of the chat input with an animation as it is asked, the message list giving way above it. While the harness works on a question, it is a single row showing the latest thing the harness did. A finished question is a row with its status and first line.
132	However many questions are asked, the stack is only as tall as its rows, up to 240 pixels, the queue's most, and scrolls beyond that with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), kept on the newest question, nearest the tabs, as each is asked. Once it holds more than fit, the stack lays out only the rows in view, as a table does, so a long stack costs no more to show, scroll, or animate than a short one, and the drawer's bottom follows the stack's top as ever.
133	Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status and first line, above its full task table, in the [AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope), which it fills, the table scrolling once it is taller, with its lock to the bottom off to start with. Only one question is open at a time: opening another closes the one open back down to its row. An open question leaves the stack for the drawer. Clicking an open question's heading closes it down to its row in the stack, and clicking a finished question's row opens it again. Each question has a close button, which removes it and stops it if it is still running, leaving the others running. A closed question becomes a previous answer.
134	
135	#### Answer Steps
136	
137	For a question, only the answer matters, so wherever a finished question's task table is shown, an open question and a previous answer, the table collapses the steps leading up to the answer, as the [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A question closed into the previous answers starts collapsed again. Tasks are never collapsed like this: see the [MessageList](../message-list/index.md#message-list).
138	
139	#### Previous Answers
140	
141	Previous answers are a [HistoryListScope](../../../ui/components/history-list/index.md#history-list-scope), shown only while the Ask tab is selected, at the top of the questions stacked above the tabs. It lists every question asked before and closed: those saved with the project and those closed since. Its row reads "No previous answers", "1 previous answer", or "N previous answers", and while expanded, "Back to the questions". Each previous answer offers Resend, which asks its question again, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. Expanded, the row and the list go into the [AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope), sliding up from on top of any question rows still in the stack. The questions asked from now on carry on the conversation the latest of them left off.
142	
143	#### Answer Drawer
144	
145	[AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope)
146	
147	#### Selecting Answer Text
148	
149	The text of an answer being viewed, in the answer drawer, whether an open question or a previous answer, can be selected by dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects text ending within the drawer shows a [SelectionPopoverScope](../../../ui/components/selection-popover/index.md#selection-popover-scope) with two buttons: "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a paperclip icon.
150	Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard. Attach to prompt adds it to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the selection. The popover also closes when the drawer closes.
151	
152	#### Attachments
153	
154	What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.
155	Images can be attached too: pasted from the clipboard while the chat input has focus, dropped onto the chat input from the file manager, or chosen with a small ghost button with an image icon, whose tooltip says "Attach images", on the tab row between the last tab and the help text, which opens the platform's file picker for any files, several at once, since the picker can't be limited to images. Pasting an image attaches it rather than putting anything in the text, even when the clipboard holds text as well; every image on the clipboard is attached, and a clipboard with no image pastes its text as usual. Several files dropped or chosen at once are attached in their order, each on its own merits. An image is known by its content, not its name, and only PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP are taken: anything else pasted, dropped, or chosen, BMP, TIFF, and SVG included, is not attached, and a warning notification titled "Not attached" says it isn't an image. An image larger than 5 MB is not attached either, and the same notification says it is too large. A folder dropped or chosen isn't an image either, and a file that can't be read is not attached, the same notification saying it couldn't be read, and why. Each file left out has its own notification, and the others are still attached.
156	Files can be dropped only on the chat input itself, its tabs, the attachments, and the text input; dropping them on the message list above it does nothing. While files are dragged over the chat input, its background is highlighted with the accent's fill, laid about a quarter of the way over it.
157	An attached image's row shows a small thumbnail, its file name, or "Pasted image" for one pasted, and its size in pixels, muted, with the same remove button; hovering the thumbnail shows the image larger, at most 320 pixels. Images and text are listed together in the order they were attached while the prompt is written. A prompt taken back into the input, as when a queued prompt is edited, lists its text first, then its images, each image named by its saved file, a pasted one included.
158	Attachments belong to the prompt being written, not to a tab: switching tabs keeps them all, and they go with the prompt whichever tab it is sent from. When the prompt is sent, its attachments are sent along with it and the list empties, as the text input does. A queued prompt keeps the attachments it was sent with.
159	
160	#### Projects
161	
162	The questions stacked above the tabs, the open answer, and the previous answers belong to their project, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says: switching projects shows those of the project switched to, while the questions of other projects carry on running in the background. The prompt being written, its attachments, the selected tab, and the Slice toggle stay as they are across a switch, and are sent to the project on screen.
163	
164	#### Escape
165	
166	Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat input. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS) brings it back, from anywhere the chat input isn't beneath something else, as the [MainWindowScope](../../application/MainWindow.md#main-window-scope) says.
167	
168	#### Grow To Fit
169	
170	The text input is a [GrowingTextInputScope](../../../ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input-scope) growing to 12 rows at most. Its single row lines up with the send button.
171	
172	#### Auto Focus
173	
174	The chat input should be auto-focused.
175	
176	#### Syntax Highlighting
177	
178	Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)
179	
180	#### Lsp
181	
182	[LSP](../../lsp/index.md#lsp)
183	
184	#### Harness Mentions
185	
186	```
187	overview: Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@` offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself. The placeholder mentions both.
188	trigger: A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter, digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one they never reach the [LSP](../../lsp/index.md#lsp).
189	offered: The skills, commands, and agents offered are the [HarnessCatalogScope](../../harness-integration/catalog/index.md#harness-catalog-scope)'s. Each shows whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as documentation when it has one. Results are narrowed and ordered like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before matches anywhere in it, then by name.
190	accepting: Accepting one inserts it as a mention, as the [HarnessCatalogScope](../../harness-integration/catalog/index.md#harness-catalog-scope) says, in place of what was typed of it. Mentions work without the [LSP](../../lsp/index.md#lsp).
191	```
192	
193	#### Hidden Anchor
194	
195	While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes, they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope)
196	
197	##### Escaping
198	
199	A prompt may hold anything, text pasted into it included, so it isn't written into the anchor as Piton prose, where braces, colons, leading dashes, code fences, comments, indentation, and backslashes all mean something. The anchor is exported, so that it compiles, and its userPrompt is a multi-line escape block, which Piton keeps exactly as it is: the prompt's lines, each at the block's indentation, fenced by a line of three backslashes, or of one more than any line of the prompt made only of backslashes, so nothing in it closes the block early. The systemPrompt is written the same way.
200	Each at-brace or dollar-brace around a dotted path of identifiers whose first name is imported, in the userPrompt and then the systemPrompt, is also listed once, in the order they first appear, as an item of the anchor's references property, left out when there are none; a reference to a name that isn't imported, such as a pasted shell variable, is only text. `piton compile` resolves the references. What the harness receives is the prompt as it was saved, line for line, with each reference replaced by what it resolved to: a dollar-brace by its text, and an at-brace by a Markdown link, from the project directory, to the reference document the project's build writes for it, in the reference root of the config's first adapter, such as .claude/reference, named by its dotted path, and going to the heading for the anchor or property it names once the document is built. A prompt saved by an earlier version, as quoted pieces or as prose, still reads back.
201	
202	##### Auto Imports
203	
204	The names a prompt uses are imported however the prompt got there, typed, completed, or pasted. What `piton lsp` is shown while the prompt is typed is the prompt as prose, line for line and position for position as typed, but with anything outside a reference other than letters, digits, and spaces between words blanked out, character for character. Pasted text with an unclosed quote or brace, a code fence, deeper indentation, or what would be a comment then never stops the server finding the names that need importing, both as completions are offered and when the prompt is sent.
205	
206	##### Attached Text
207	
208	A prompt with attached text gives the hidden anchor an attachedText
209	
210	###### Property
211	
212	a list with an item per attached piece of text, in the
213	
214	order they were attached, keyed text1, text2, and so on. Since attached text is taken as it is, not as Piton, each is written as a multi-line escape block, as the userPrompt is, so nothing in it is interpolated or evaluated. A prompt with nothing attached has no attachedText property.
215
